# Test review rules

Scope: every test target that `cargo test` runs (unit tests in `src/`, integration tests under `tests/`, and doctests), their helpers, and tests embedded in `<crate>/src/examples`. Benchmarks are out of scope. End-to-end or system tests that need provisioned services, credentials, or dedicated CI jobs are also out of scope: such coverage requires a separate design document defining purpose, boundaries, prerequisites, isolation, and runtime budget, so do not suggest it ad hoc.

This guide is the repository's test policy. Within its scope it takes precedence over the convention rule in `SKILL.md`: request these forms even where Clippy permits alternatives. Apply them to tests that the pull request adds or changes; do not request cleanup of unrelated existing tests.

## Determinism first

**Determinism is the primary focus.** A test must reach the same verdict from the same controlled inputs, independent of test order, parallel tests, host state, and timing. Determinism also makes tests fast: a test that avoids real I/O, wall-clock timers, network access, and subprocesses runs in-process in microseconds and never needs retries.

Adding test-only APIs to achieve this is justified. Code that performs I/O or system calls, reads clocks, or uses randomness should be mockable ([M-MOCKABLE-SYSCALLS](https://microsoft.github.io/rust-guidelines/guidelines/libs/resilience/#M-MOCKABLE-SYSCALLS)), with the testing surface behind a test feature ([M-TEST-UTIL](https://microsoft.github.io/rust-guidelines/guidelines/libs/resilience/#M-TEST-UTIL)). When no existing seam controls a dependency, recommend adding one.

## Review sequence

1. Read the changed tests, their setup and cleanup, and the exercised production path. Identify the contract and every uncontrolled dependency.
2. Check input control, state isolation, and synchronization first, then assertions.
3. Exercise the contract through the narrowest API that owns it, with collaborators mocked; prefer the public API from `tests/` when it suffices. For concurrency, verify invariants across explored schedules, not one fixed schedule.
4. Report only evidenced defects: cite the source, name the wrong outcome or uncontrolled dependency, and recommend the smallest fix that preserves coverage. Skip style nits.

Passing CI, stable snapshots, stress reruns, or a closed bug do not prove determinism or a root-cause fix. Distinguish harness defects from product races, and preserve security checks and meaningful assertions.

Markers in the tables are search hints, not proof of a defect; check actual usage and imported aliases.

## Control inputs and state

| Avoid | Use instead |
| --- | --- |
| Network services, host configuration, installed tools, sign-in, browsers, or developer credentials. Markers: `reqwest::`, `TcpStream::connect`, `UdpSocket::bind`. | Mock service and host dependencies; derive expectations from controlled inputs, not machine configuration. |
| Running external processes or generated fake executables. Markers: `Command::new`, `.spawn()`, `.output()`, `.sh`, `.bat`. | Mock the process runner with scripted status, stdout, and stderr; test command construction, parsing, and policy in-process. An integration test under `tests/` may run the crate's own binary (`env!("CARGO_BIN_EXE_<name>")`) when the CLI contract is the subject; pass explicit arguments, environment, working directory, and stdin. |
| Unspecified collaborators silently succeeding or reaching the host. | Reject unexpected calls; script only the interactions the scenario needs. |
| Wall-clock or random values, or sleeps used for ordering. Markers: `SystemTime::now`, `Instant::now`, `Utc::now`, `thread_rng`, `rand::rng`, `sleep`. | Inject a [tick](https://docs.rs/tick/latest/tick/) clock: `tick::Clock::new_frozen` (feature `test-util`) for fixed time, and `ClockControl` to advance time explicitly in timer tests. Seed or script randomness. Synchronize with channels, barriers, or notifications. |
| Writing input fixtures to disk during test setup. Markers: `fs::write`, `File::create`, `create_dir_all`. | Prefer in-memory values, byte buffers, or injected readers. If a file fixture is required, commit it as source and read it unchanged (`include_str!`, `include_bytes!`, or a checked-in path). Do not generate fixture files at test runtime. |
| Shared mutable fixtures, caches, or output directories. | Own mutable state per test; share only immutable inputs. When writing files is the behavior under test, give each test its own output directory. |
| Global-state interference or first-use ordering hidden by atomics, save/restore, or partial locks. Markers: `static`, `AtomicUsize`, `thread_local!`, `set_hook`, `set_global_default`. | Inject owned state. Initialize unavoidable shared infrastructure deterministically before concurrent tests, and isolate observations per test. Thread-local state works only if all observed work stays on that thread. Resetting state afterward does not prevent concurrent interference; unavoidable global mutation needs a separate test design. |
| Process environment or working-directory mutation, or host-dependent fixture paths. Markers: `set_var`, `remove_var`, `set_current_dir`, `current_dir`. | Pass environment and working directory as explicit inputs; use synthetic paths for mocked I/O or stable checked-in fixture paths. |
| Permission changes, lock races, mandatory privileges, or host-dependent filesystem metadata. Markers: `set_permissions`, `symlink`. | Mock filesystem operations and metadata, or inject specific errors. Preserve production security checks instead of relaxing them for fixtures. |

## Assert exact outcomes

| Avoid | Use instead |
| --- | --- |
| Substring assertions instead of checking the whole result. Markers: `assert!(x.contains(...))`. | Prefer full `insta` snapshots or exact string or structured equality. Control inputs; normalize only incidental values. Use `starts_with` for prefix contracts and check any meaningful remainder. Use `contains` only when containment itself is the contract. |
| Negative tests that accept any error or generic error text. Markers: `.is_err()`, `.unwrap_err().to_string()`. | Use `.unwrap_err()` or `.expect_err()` and assert the typed cause and its fields after setup reaches the intended branch. Test exact error wording separately with deterministic inputs. |
| Boolean checks that discard values or errors, or verify only nonempty output. Markers: `.is_ok()`, `.is_some()`, `.is_none()`, `assert!(!x.is_empty())`, `.success()`, `.failure()`. | For expected `Ok` or `Some`, use `.unwrap()` or `.expect()` and compare the value. For expected `None`, use `assert_eq!(actual, None)` or `let None = actual else { panic!("expected None") };`. Also assert relevant state changes and side effects. |
| Branching on the actual result instead of asserting one expected variant. Markers: `match` or `if let` on the value under test, wildcard arms. | Use `let Enum::A(x) = actual else { panic!("expected A") };`, then assert the payload. Split distinct expected outcomes into separate cases; fail on unexpected variants instead of adapting assertions to them. |
| Assertions tied to compiler implementation details. Markers: allocation counts, `Backtrace`, `#[inline`, `black_box`. | Assert observable behavior that holds in both debug and release builds, not assumed stack layout, allocation counts, or call sites. Require such properties only when they are the explicit API contract; `black_box` does not guarantee them. |

## Keep tests cheap and in place

| Avoid | Use instead |
| --- | --- |
| Tests embedded in demonstration examples under `<crate>/src/examples`. Markers: `#[test]`, `#[tokio::test]`, or `#[cfg(test)]` in `src/examples/`. | Keep examples focused on demonstration. Put regression tests in test modules or `tests/` targets that the CI `cargo test` gate runs; do not count example-embedded tests as coverage. |
| Requiring a full pipeline to test a utility. | Call the utility directly with deterministic mocked collaborators. |
| Mocking the behavior being asserted. | Mock only dependencies; run the real code under test. Reports, probes, and policies can be mocked when they are dependencies, not the subject. |
| Test helpers exposed in default APIs. Markers: test-only `pub` items outside `#[cfg(test)]`, `default =` in `[features]`. | Keep private helpers in `#[cfg(test)]` modules. Gate exported helpers behind a non-default test feature ([M-TEST-UTIL](https://microsoft.github.io/rust-guidelines/guidelines/libs/resilience/#M-TEST-UTIL)) that workspace defaults do not enable. |
| Slow or unbounded test work, or machine-speed assertions. Markers: `.elapsed()`, `timeout`, large iteration counts, `loom::model`. | Target under one second per test, excluding compilation. Reduce fixtures and work, and mock expensive dependencies. Bound loops and explored schedules while preserving the invariant, and state exploration limits. Assert work bounds, not wall-clock cutoffs; deadlines are only safety limits. |
| Blanket Miri exclusions for one unsupported dependency. Markers: `cfg(not(miri))` on whole modules, `cfg_attr(miri, ignore)` without a reason. | Ignore only affected tests, each with a reason; keep unaffected tests enabled. |
| Untuned stress workloads under Miri. Markers: `stress`, repeated loops, large iteration counts. | Exclude stress workloads with a reasoned `#[cfg_attr(miri, ignore = "...")]`, or reduce the Miri workload and measure its runtime. Keep a small invariant-focused Miri case; native speed does not predict interpreter cost. |
| Retries, longer sleeps or timeouts, weaker assertions, ignored tests, or nonrecurrence presented as fixes. Markers: `retry`, `#[ignore]`. | Remove the evidenced uncontrolled dependency while preserving coverage. Keep unresolved product races under investigation. A temporary quarantine must name the lost coverage, an owner, and the restoration condition. |
